title: Museum and gallery engagement varies sharply by English local area, with physical and digital access following different geographies
source_unit: Department for Culture, Media and Sport, Community and Engagement Survey 2025/26: museums and galleries
geography: England; adults aged 16 and over, national and local-authority estimates

observations.period: 2025/26; museum or gallery engagement in the previous 12 months by local authority

denominator.unit: Community and Engagement Survey responses across England; local-authority estimates are survey-weighted population estimates

engaged_any.unit: percent of adults engaging with museums or galleries at least once

physical_engagement_england.unit: percent of adults physically visiting a museum or gallery

physical_local_authority_high.unit: percent in the City of London

physical_local_authority_gap.unit: percentage-point difference between reported high and low local-authority estimates

mechanism.value: Physical cultural access is strongly place-differentiated, but the local-authority spread is a composite of supply, tourism, transport, population composition, income, education, and self-selection rather than a pure venue effect

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from the DCMS Community and Engagement Survey 2025/26 museums and galleries report; local-authority high and low values are published rounded estimates.
observations.uncertainty: Estimates are rounded and survey-weighted; the release cautions that subnational differences should be interpreted with confidence intervals and that local authority is an area classification, not an individual treatment.
observations.subgroup: Adults aged 16 and over in England, by lower-tier or unitary local authority.
observations.counterinterpretation: The City of London estimate may reflect tourism and unusual population composition, while Blackburn with Darwen may differ in age, deprivation, transport, education, or survey response; neither endpoint identifies the mechanism.

observations.period: 2025/26; physical and digital museum or gallery engagement and subgroup contrasts

denominator.unit: Community and Engagement Survey responses across England; estimates are survey-weighted population shares

digital_engagement_england.unit: percent of adults digitally engaging with museums or galleries

digital_local_authority_gap.unit: percentage-point difference between reported high and low local-authority estimates

engagement_overlap.value: Among all adults, 12% engaged both physically and digitally, 30% physically only, and 3% digitally only

disability_physical_gap.unit: percentage-point difference: 45% non-disabled versus 38% disabled physically engaged

mechanism.value: Digital engagement is a smaller but rising access channel and does not simply replace physical engagement: most engagement is physical-only, while digital rates also vary sharply by place and are only slightly different by disability status

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from the DCMS 2025/26 museums and galleries report; local-authority and subgroup gaps are calculated from published rounded estimates.
observations.uncertainty: Physical and digital measures cover different activities and may include multiple engagements; the annual period combines April-September Participation Survey data with October-March Community and Engagement Survey data, and the report notes sample-size and weighting limitations.
observations.subgroup: Adults aged 16 and over in England, with physical/digital and disability-status breakdowns.
observations.counterinterpretation: Digital engagement may complement rather than substitute for visits; disability differences may reflect transport, health, venue design, age, income, or reporting, while local digital gaps may reflect language, broadband, institutional presence, or survey composition.

related_sources.claim: DCMS release guidance describing the survey, coverage, replacement of prior surveys, geographic levels, period, and supplementary documentation.
ONS local-statistics route using the 2025/26 Community and Engagement Survey and showing local cultural-engagement data-download infrastructure.
DCMS museums and galleries statistical-release landing route and report/data-table publication family.

boundary: This record adds an England local-area, museum/galleries, physical/digital engagement layer. It does not establish venue supply, travel time, affordability, cultural belonging, service quality, causal local-authority effects, or that digital access substitutes for physical attendance.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: DCMS museums and galleries report and related survey guidance reviewed; national, local-authority, physical/digital, overlap, disability, annual-period, sample, rounding, and confidence-interval notes checked.
